study.design: Retrospective active-comparator cohort within a federated OMOP common data model network of 15 Korean tertiary hospitals, with Cyclops regularized propensity-score estimation, 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching, site-stratified Cox regression at a postacute (31-3650 day) primary risk window, and empirical calibration against 54 negative-control outcomes

data_source.name: federated OMOP common data model network of 15 Korean tertiary hospitals

inclusion: Incident appendectomy (target), cholecystectomy (first active comparator), or hernia repair (second active comparator) between 2002-01-01 and 2024-12-31
At least 365 days of observation before the index date
At least 1 day of observation after the index date
exclusion: Prior diagnosis of organ-specific neoplasm: appendix neoplasm (concept 4129881 + descendants) for appendectomy; gallbladder neoplasm (concept 4130520 + descendants) for cholecystectomy; no neoplasm-of-organ exclusion for hernia repair
Any concurrent same-day major abdominal surgery from an 8-concept set including hysterectomy, cesarean section, colon excision, oophorectomy, salpingectomy, and descendants
Any of the 35 biomarker-abnormality events in the -365 to -30 day prior-abnormality-exclusion window (symmetric across arms)

comparators.name: cholecystectomy
comparators.rationale: First active surgical comparator: distinct surgical indication (biliary disease) sharing general perioperative care patterns with appendectomy

comparators.name: hernia_repair
comparators.rationale: Second active surgical comparator: elective non-abdominal-organ surgery distinguishing appendix-specific biology from generic perioperative effects

exposure.operationalization: OMOP standard concepts with descendants: appendectomy 4198190 (ATLAS cohort 1072); cholecystectomy 4242997 (cohort 1074); hernia repair 4196678 and 4244809 (cohort 1121). First occurrence per patient.

primary.name: Three-endpoint cellular-immune core: low lymphocyte percentage, neutrophilia, elevated WBC
primary.definition: First post-index laboratory measurement crossing a prespecified threshold; pooled across measurement-recording variants where applicable

primary.name: Supportive inflammatory endpoint: CRP elevated (mg/dL + mg/L pooled)
primary.definition: First post-index CRP measurement above the prespecified threshold; events pooled across CRP mg/dL and mg/L unit variants

secondary.name: 30 prespecified biomarker abnormality endpoints across cellular-immune, inflammatory, hematologic, hepatobiliary, metabolic (glucose, lipids), endocrine, and renal domains
secondary.definition: First post-index measurement crossing the prespecified assay-specific reference limit or clinical-decision cutoff; 5 analytes bidirectional; 3 endpoints pool measurement-recording variants

secondary.name: 11 prespecified clinical disease outcomes
secondary.definition: Ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease, asthma, atopic dermatitis, rheumatoid arthritis, C. difficile infection, Parkinson disease, biliary calculus, colorectal cancer, acute MI (v2 without inpatient-only requirement), type-2 diabetes (v3 laboratory-confirmed: concept code OR glucose >=126 mg/dL OR HbA1c >=6.5%)

negative_controls.selection: Prespecified OHDSI LEGEND framework drawing on Voss et al. and Ryan et al. reference sets
negative_controls.criteria: No plausible causal link to appendectomy or either comparator; coverage of at least 8 OMOP body systems; at least 1 event in at least 80% of sites
negative_controls.note: Clinical domain negative controls — addresses broad residual systematic error rather than laboratory-specific measurement-process bias

covariates: Prior conditions (long-term lookback, all OMOP standard concepts in CDM)
Site indicator (dummy variable to encode institutional heterogeneity)

analysis.matching: 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity-score matching on logit propensity score; caliper width 0.2 standard deviations of logit propensity score
analysis.primary_model: Site-stratified Cox proportional-hazards regression with standard partial-likelihood variance
analysis.calibration: Empirical calibration against 54 negative-control outcomes; per-comparator empirical null fitted by method of moments (Schuemie 2014); calibrated HR = exp(logHR - null_mean); calibrated SE = sqrt(SE^2 + null_sd^2); calibrated 95% CI and P-value derived from calibrated SE
sensitivity: Lookback 90/365/unlimited outer windows with 30-day inner skip
Beta secondary window: 1-3650 days (including 1-30 day acute interval)

hypotheses.primary: Appendectomy is associated with reproducible, multi-sensitivity-robust differences in cellular-immune and inflammatory laboratory abnormality event rates beyond the postacute landmark across both active comparators (cholecystectomy and hernia repair)
secondary: Clinical disease incidence (UC, Crohn, atopic dermatitis, type-2 diabetes, Parkinson disease, colorectal cancer, etc.) differs after appendectomy versus active comparators in the postacute window
The cross-comparator core findings are robust to sensitivity analyses (LOSO, sigma-grid, lookback variation, beta secondary window)
